title: The Identification Configuration Without the Logotype
slide_intent: Teach designers to separate the mark from the door lettering when a different surface gives it a better display. The remaining door information must still read as a single identification.
strategic_value: NASA can use more of a vehicle’s body for recognition without losing the government, agency and facility information on the front doors.
demonstration: A small passenger-door inset places the text in context. The enlarged door diagram gives heights and spacing for the government and agency lines and center or facility name, all on a common left edge.
practical_value: Use the text-only door arrangement when the logotype is displayed elsewhere on the vehicle. Check both door hardware and the line breaks of a long facility name.

content_islands.name: Placement explanation
content_islands.spec: Use two short text columns beside the heading to state where the mark and remaining identification go.

content_islands.name: Passenger-door inset
content_islands.spec: Draw the complete door at lower left and place the lettering in the clear area below the window.

content_islands.name: Dimensioned lettering
content_islands.spec: Enlarge the door at right. Show the mirror, handle and text block with measurement marks, retaining the common left alignment through a multiline facility name.
